# Frontier Data Lead

## About the Role

The Frontier Data Lead (FDL) is the Managing Director’s program lead for client delivery and a key driver of account growth. A program is a set of projects in one domain with one goal, and a client can have several. You run those programs, make sure clients are never surprised, and keep our systems accurate. You also understand each partner’s goals and organization deeply, connect them with our growth and research teams, and find where we can help next.

## What You’ll Do

### Client Delivery and Communication

- Be the proactive point of contact for every account, so no client has to ask “what’s the status?”
- Send regular updates on progress, volumes, quality, blockers, and milestones.
- Flag risks, delays, and scope changes early, with a proposed path forward.
- Run client check-ins covering delivery and what’s next, and capture decisions and action items.

### Partner Insight and Account Growth

- Understand each partner’s research goals, model roadmap, and data priorities, and keep that view current.
- Map and build relationships across each partner’s organization, beyond your day-to-day contacts.
- Spot expansion opportunities early and work with the growth team to turn them into scoped proposals.
- Own an account plan for each partner: goals, stakeholders, current footprint, and next actions.
- Lead quarterly business reviews centered on the partner’s goals, not only our delivery metrics.

### Research Bridge

- Share partner needs and recurring data challenges with our research team to inform its agenda.
- Bring our research insights and roadmap to partners in ways that connect to their goals.
- Facilitate working sessions between partner teams and our researchers where there’s shared interest.

### Operations and Systems

- Maintain a single, current view of every account, program, and project: status, owner, timeline, and open issues.
- Track client requests and spec changes through resolution, and confirm with engineers that project setup matches what was agreed.
- Keep the CRM, trackers, and account plans accurate, and audit them regularly.
- Prepare reporting for the Managing Director and leadership on delivery health and account growth.
- Build lightweight templates and ensure clean handoffs between sales, project setup, and delivery.

## What We’re Looking For

- 3+ years in consulting, program management, account management, or client operations, ideally running several client engagements at once.
- Excellent written communication and comfort being the face of delivery, including delivering hard news with a plan.
- Strong organization and attention to detail across multiple accounts.
- A consultative, curious approach and a track record of expanding client relationships.
- Ability to translate between technical and business audiences, in both directions.
- Experience working closely with an executive and making decisions with incomplete information.
- Self-directed: you spot issues before they become escalations, and opportunities before they become RFPs.

## Nice to Have

- Experience with AI training data, data labeling, or managed-services delivery.
- Familiarity with how frontier AI labs and enterprise AI teams build and evaluate models.
- Familiarity with Labelbox or similar platforms.
- Comfort with light automation or no-code tools.

## What Success Looks Like

### First 90 Days

- A current inventory of every account, with status, owner, and next milestone.
- A standard update format and cadence in place for every account.
- Systems audited and up to date, with a routine to keep them that way.
- An account plan and stakeholder map for each priority partner.

### Ongoing

- Clients hear about delays, changes, and wins from us first.
- The Managing Director can see the state of any account in minutes.
- Partners bring us into their planning early, and we engage more teams within each account over time.
- Partner insights shape our research agenda, and our research regularly opens new conversations.
- A steady flow of qualified opportunities that turn into new programs.
vagas.requisitos: Own client delivery and account growth for Alignerr’s AI partners. Keep clients informed, build relationships across their orgs, and connect partner needs to our research team.

## About the Role

Alignerr is where domain experts, engineers, and creators join to work on the projects that power frontier AI. Growth Operations keeps that engine running: we find the right people, launch new data projects fast, and make sure the work that comes back is good.

We’re hiring a Growth Operations Manager: a generalist who can pick up an ambiguous problem on Monday and ship a working system by Friday. You’ll report to the Director of Growth Operations and work closely with engineering, product, legal, and delivery teams.

**Location:** [Remote / hybrid, to be confirmed]

**Compensation:** [Range to be added]

## What You’ll Do

- Turn client briefs into live projects, from scoping and decisions through contributor instructions and recruiting.
- Build and run sourcing and screening pipelines for specialized talent, across domains and languages.
- Dig into the data to find out why contributors drop off or quality slips, then work with product and engineering to fix it.
- Turn one-off work into templates, trackers, and playbooks that other people can run without you.
- Keep leadership informed on contributor supply, quality, and project health.

## What We’re Looking For

- 4-8 years in growth, operations, strategy, marketplace operations, recruiting operations, or a similar generalist role, ideally at a startup or scale-up.
- A track record of owning ambiguous, cross-functional projects from zero to shipped.
- Strong analytical skills: fluent in spreadsheets, comfortable with SQL or willing to learn fast, and able to make sense of large, messy datasets.
- Excellent written communication, with the ability to explain complex things simply.
- Good judgment on when to move fast and when to pull in legal, security, or quality.
- High ownership and a bias to action.

## Nice to Have

- Experience with marketplaces, talent platforms, crowdsourcing, or AI training data.
- Recruiting or sourcing experience at volume, including niche or technical talent.
- Multilingual ability or experience with global communities.
- Scripting or automation skills (for example Python, or AI tools to scale repetitive work).

## What Success Looks Like

- **First 30 days:** you’ve learned the platform and taken ownership of a defined workstream.
- **First 90 days:** you’ve independently launched a project or pipeline and moved a key metric.
- **First 6 months:** you’re the go-to owner for a strategic area, with systems others can run.

Mercor is seeking experienced Portuguese Linguistic Experts to join a cutting-edge AI research project in partnership with a leading research lab. This role centers on evaluating how effectively a large language model (LLM) performs in Portuguese-language tasks and on curating high-quality Portuguese linguistic data to train and improve the model's understanding and generation capabilities.

**Key Responsibilities:**
- Evaluate the quality and accuracy of LLM-generated Portuguese text across various use cases (e.g., translation, summarization, dialogue, grammar correction).
- Edit, refine, or rewrite Portuguese content to meet linguistic and cultural standards.
- Annotate Portuguese text for grammatical, syntactic, and semantic features.
- Identify model errors and language gaps, and collaborate with AI researchers to improve LLM performance.
- Provide detailed linguistic feedback and analysis to guide ongoing model training efforts.

**You're a strong fit if you have:**
- Native or near-native fluency in Portuguese, with excellent command over grammar, syntax, and stylistics.
- Professional experience in translation, editing, linguistic annotation, or NLP data work in Portuguese.
- Strong understanding of linguistic nuances, regional variations, and context-appropriate usage.
- Interest in AI and LLM-driven language technologies (preferred but not required).
- Excellent attention to detail and ability to spot subtle errors or unnatural phrasing.
- Clear communication skills and experience working in distributed, remote teams.

**Why Join**
- Contribute to cutting-edge AI research in partnership with a leading research lab.
- Work on high-impact projects that directly support the development of advanced AI systems.
- Gain hands-on exposure to state-of-the-art AI research and development.
- Join a fast-moving project where your expertise and judgment can have a meaningful impact.

About Turing 
 Turing is one of the world’s fastest-growing AI companies, accelerating the advancement and deployment of powerful AI systems.
 Turing helps customers in two ways: Working with the world’s leading AI labs to advance frontier model capabilities in thinking, reasoning, coding, agentic behavior, multimodality, multilinguality, STEM, and frontier knowledge; and leveraging that work to build real-world AI systems that solve mission-critical priorities for companies.

 Role Overview 
 We are looking for a Merchandising & Category Management Subject Matter Expert (SME) to design, evaluate, and calibrate high-fidelity domain tasks, retail scenarios, and benchmark solutions.
 Depending on your depth of retail experience, candidates will be considered for an Expert Contributor (Merchandising / Category Manager) or a Senior Specialist / Reviewer (Senior Merchandising / Category Manager) track within our functional evaluation pods.

 Requirements 
 • Experience: 3–15 years of hands-on experience in retail merchandising, buying, category management, or inventory allocation.

• Core Competencies: 
 • Demonstrated expertise in assortment architecture, product allocation, and merchandise financial planning.

• Practical experience creating and analyzing assortment plans, visual planograms, and promotional calendars.

• Strong command of foundational retail calculations (GMROI, turn, markdowns, margin impact, weeks of supply).

• Execution & Communication: 
 • Proven ability to work under peer review, adapt quickly to calibration feedback, and adhere to structured rubrics.

• Strong written communication skills to articulate clear solution rationales and step-by-step methodology breakdowns.

 Responsibilities 
 • Benchmark Task Authoring: Design realistic, high-difficulty retail exercises, assortment planning scenarios, promotional strategy models, and planogram challenges with gold-standard solution sets.

• Rubric Application & Scoring: Apply evaluation rubrics established by the Functional SME (Expert) Lead to systematically assess and score retail planning submissions.

• Review & Calibration: Participate in peer calibration sessions, incorporate structured feedback, iterate on task designs, and help resolve edge cases in retail math or allocation logic.

• Commercial Modeling: Build and evaluate scenarios incorporating core retail KPIs, including sell-through rates, GMROI, open-to-buy (OTB), margin mix, and inventory turnover.

 Education & Experience 
 • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience in any field.
• Experience in AI evaluation, data annotation, content review, quality assurance, or a related analytical role is preferred but not required.
 Offer Details: 
 • Commitments Required: at least 4 hours per day and upto 40 hours per week with 4 hours of overlap with PST.
• Engagement type: Contractor
• Engagement Length: 12 weeks
 Evaluation Process -
 • Applicants needs to submit Job Interest Form & complete the assessment. 
• Final selected candidates will be contacted with the next steps and onboarding requirements.

Candidates will be placed into an Expert Contributor (mid-level) or Senior Specialist / Reviewer (senior-level) track based on overall commercial experience, deal complexity, and prior background with quality calibration or peer review.

• Iterative Refinement: Incorporate structured calibration feedback and peer critiques across sprint cycles to continuously elevate benchmark solution quality.
